recommendation: Keep this no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed unless a future work group decision changes the DocumentReference/Provenance boundary.
issue_request: FHIR-7971 was a Published FHIR-core DocumentReference change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking to explain the overlap between DocumentReference metadata and Provenance and to reference the Provenance overlap section.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied in git-svn commit 8fcdf92a9bcfbecca689270c3ef75225af7c56fa, which cites #7971 and svn revision 6203. That commit added the DocumentReference paragraph distinguishing provenance of the referenced document from provenance of the DocumentReference, and added an overlap anchor to the Provenance introduction. Later text edits, including b7f4a901e15b2e31e2ac6bbcc58b0deef2f14fa0, preserved the same substantive wording.
additional_context: Both DocumentReference and Provenance are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. The current DocumentReference introduction still explains the two sets of provenance and links to provenance.html#overlap, while the current Provenance introduction still has the overlap anchor and general overlap guidance. Jira and community searches found no later source decision that reverses this paragraph; FHIR-55558 is a later no-change issue that separately confirms some DocumentReference/Provenance overlap is intentional when the semantics differ.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already satisfies the published resolution, and adding more prose would duplicate existing guidance without changing implementer understanding.

related_jiras.note: Later no-change issue distinguishing DocumentReference relationship semantics from Provenance activity semantics.
